--- title: "Serial visual search" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · HVIS_OR_ESP_BUSQUEDA_SERIAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (E · Decision with response time; quality class B). Generated on November 28, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea HVIS_OR_ESP_BUSQUEDA_SERIAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Búsqueda serial*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/HVIS_OR_ESP_BUSQUEDA_SERIAL.html). ::: ::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"} **Class B.** It has enough data to be described, but it lacks some of the guarantees of class A (stability across time points, item-level reliability or validity). Use with caution and not for individual decisions. [What each class means](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases). ::: **In one sentence.** Serial visual search, from age 4 to 6 (2,373 administrations in 3 cohorts). AUC .58–.63 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1987 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 24 | | Task family | E · Decision with response time | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The child is instructed to say if the letter O is present, or not, among different size groups of Qs. | ![Example of the screen format (2018 screenshot; not necessarily an item from this task).](../../figuras/pantallas/formato_imagenes.png){width=45%} ## Theoretical framework **Visual-attentional span** is the number of visual elements processed simultaneously within a string. On the platform, a string of letters, numbers or symbols is briefly presented and the child chooses what they saw. **Serial search** asks whether there is an O among groups of Qs of different sizes. The **sustained attention** task (UNED battery) consists of 50 trials in which the child decides whether the name they hear matches the picture; despite its name, the catalog describes it as an index of inhibitory control. Reading requires processing several letters at once and maintaining attention along the line. **What the evidence says:** - **Visual-attentional span predicts reading beyond phonemic awareness.** In 417 French children in Grades 1, 3 and 5, it predicted reading independently of phonemic awareness, especially for irregular words [@bosse2009span]. Orthographic depth modulates how this attention is distributed: advanced bilinguals reading in French and Basque distributed it more evenly than those reading in Spanish and Basque [@antzaka2018depth]. - **Visual search is associated with reading, with small samples.** In 16 children with dyslexia and 16 controls, slow serial search was associated with visual-attentional span and with irregular word reading, not with phonology [@lallier2013search]. Visual scanning measured in preschool predicted learning to read in Italian children [@ferretti2008scanning]. - **Sustained attention is related more to comprehension than to word reading.** In 245 poor readers in Grades 4 and 5, it explained unique variance in comprehension, but not in reading accuracy or fluency [@macdonald2021sustained]. The evidence is weaker than for phonological processes and there are almost no studies in Spanish. **What our data show.** - **Letter and symbol subtests.** With 6–10 points and a single session, AUC from .47 to .61: separately they are not interpretable. - **Numbers and letters (36 items, ages 4–5).** α = .60 and AUC of .66–.67 against persistent difficulty and of .65 against later low comprehension. It is the best in the family, as expected of alphanumeric stimuli. - **Numbers (16 items).** α = .56 and almost zero stability across school years (ρ = .05–.19). AUC from .54 to .69. - **Serial search.** α = .74, ceiling of 11–20% and AUC from .58 to .63. - **Sustained attention.** Despite an α of .95, it shows no validity: extreme ceiling (median 45 out of 50), stability of ρ = .03–.16, null correlation with the other domains and AUC from .43 to .56. It should not be used until the data have been reviewed. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.3| 2013| 191|2017/18 | 578| 568| 10| 23| | 5.2| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 892| 0| 892| 35| | 6.2| 2010| 155|2016/17 | 903| 265| 638| 34| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|-------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.3| 568| 2013| 20.21| 3.73| 21| -2.01| 0.35| 11.09| | 6.2| 265| 2010| 21.01| 4.29| 22| -3.23| 2.26| 20.00| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|-------:| | 4.3| 568|6.7–24 |0–24 | | | 6.2| 265|0–24 |0–24 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .74. ## Validity **Concurrent.** Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Phonological awareness (4.3, r = .31); Phonological awareness (5.2, r = .31); Phonological awareness (6.2, r = .21). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .58–.63. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .56–.65. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_OR_ESP_BUSQUEDA_SERIAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .53–.67 (3 time points; 118–271 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|-------:|--:|---:|----:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.3| 568| 2013| 12| 16| 18.0| 19| 21| 23| 24| | 5.2| 892| 2011| 13| 17| 19.0| 20| 22| 23| 24| | 6.2| 265| 2010| 13| 18| 19.2| 21| 22| 23| 24| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_HVIS_OR_ESP_BUSQUEDA_SERIAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|---:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.3| 578| 0.056| 0.182| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.3| 575| 0.028| 0.732| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.3| 578| 0.035| 0.402| |School (ICC) | 4.3| 578| 0.132| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 891| 0.100| 0.003| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 890| 0.001| 0.984| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 886| 0.093| 0.005| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 892| 0.145| | |School SES (ρ) | 6.2| 903| 0.160| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 6.2| 901| 0.064| 0.335| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 6.2| 900| 0.026| 0.432| |School (ICC) | 6.2| 903| 0.148| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Serial visual search” (code 1987; LEEDUCA battery) assesses spatial orienting and visual search. Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 24 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011 and 2013 cohorts it was administered in 3 sessions, from 4 to 6 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .74 (N = 1,266, 24 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .56–.65. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 6.2 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
